:::{#def-kfold}
#### $k$-fold cross-validation

In **$k$-fold cross-validation**:

1. The data are randomly divided into $k$ [folds](#def-folds) of equal, or nearly equal, size.
2. For each fold $\fold{j}$, $j = 1, \ldots, k$:
   - Fit the model to all data *except* fold $\fold{j}$,
     giving the [fold-out rule](#def-fold-out-rule) $\fittedwo{j}{\cdot}$.
   - Compute predicted values for the observations in fold $\fold{j}$.
3. Compute a summary prediction-error measure across all folds.

:::

::: notes
If data are limited,
$k$-fold cross-validation
can replace the single validation set of @def-data-splits
for more stable tuning.
In @exr-kfold, $k = 4$ folds of 8 cars each
give 4 fits on 24 cars each.
:::
